sections.h2: Where is the Highland County Recorder's office in Hillsboro?
sections.html:
The Highland County Recorder is at 119 Governor Foraker Place, Suite 108, in Hillsboro. Mail goes to P.O. Box 804, Hillsboro, OH 45133. The county's recorder page gives 937-393-9954 and weekday hours of 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM.

One rule catches people who show up late in the day. Documents received after 3:30 PM are not recorded that day. They are held and run on the next business day, so a seller racing a closing deadline should arrive well before the office closes.

The same building houses the auditor, whose address is 119 Governor Foraker Place, with a phone of 937-393-1915 and hours of 8:00 am to 4:00 pm. Hillsboro is the county seat and the largest city in a county of about 553 square miles, so a seller in Greenfield, Lynchburg or a rural township makes the trip here for recording.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Highland County?
sections.html:
The recorder's page prints a flat price by page count, marked as the rates effective January 1, 2025. A deed of one or two pages costs $39, and each added page costs $8 more.

Highland County Recorder rates effective January 1, 2025, from the county recorder's page

4$55.00

8$87.00

The office takes cash or check for recordings. Credit cards are not accepted. Add $4.00 for each marginal notation, and expect a $12.00 charge per UCC form plus $4.00 per name, which applies only when the filing involves real estate and carries a full legal description.

sections.h2: Which formatting mistakes add a charge or cause a rejection?
sections.html:
Highland County applies Ohio's document standards from section 317.114 of the Revised Code. Any document notarized after July 1, 2009 that does not follow the standards draws an extra $20.00. The county's rules list is short, and a seller can avoid the charge with a few habits:

  • Print the deed on paper between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Keep the type at ten points or larger, in black or blue ink only, with no highlighting.
  • Leave a three-inch top margin on the first page for the recorder, auditor and engineer stamps, and a smaller top margin on later pages.
  • Enclose a self-addressed, stamped envelope if you want the original mailed back after recording.

The county also posts a conveyance standards sheet on the auditor's side of the building. Read it before the deed is drafted, because a rejection by the tax map office or the auditor costs a second trip even when there is no money penalty.

sections.h2: How does a conveyance move through the Highland County offices?
sections.html:
The county publishes a recording procedure that sends a deed through four hands, and the order matters. You bring the packet to the Recorder's Office first for a quick check that the document is recordable and the fees are right. You then visit the Auditor, who confirms the forms and the conveyance fee, and return the packet to the recorder with payment and contact details.

Inside the building the packet then goes to the Tax Map office, which checks it against county rules and stamps it or rejects it for correction. The Auditor reviews it again, and the Recorder finalizes the recording and calls you for pickup or mails it back in your envelope. A seller in a hurry should ask the title company whether it will carry the packet in person.

The Highland County Auditor's forms page lists the Ohio paperwork: DTE 100 for the real property conveyance fee statement and receipt, DTE 100EX when an exemption applies, DTE 101 for homestead property, and DTE 102 for property in the current agricultural use valuation program. Its tools menu also carries a conveyance fee calculator that includes a parcel transfer fee, so ask the auditor's staff to confirm any figure it gives you.

sections.h2: What state fees apply before the deed reaches the recorder?
sections.html:
Under section 319.202, the buyer's statement of value goes to the auditor before the deed is endorsed. The seller pays the fee set by section 319.54(G)(3), which is $1 or ten cents for each $100 or fraction of $100 of value, whichever is greater.

A county may add a real property transfer tax of no more than thirty cents per $100 under section 322.02, after two public hearings by the commissioners. The Highland County Auditor can tell you whether the county has one. Several exemptions from the statement fee exist, among them gifts between spouses or between a parent and a child, transfers for no consideration, sales for delinquent taxes and transfers that only secure a debt.

Farmland needs one more answer. The statement must say whether the parcel was in the current agricultural use valuation program, and the county's agricultural FAQ says land removed from the program owes a recoupment charge equal to three years of tax savings.

sections.h2: How can Highland County owners watch for deed fraud?
sections.html:
The recorder's page links two guides called Fraud Sleuth Instructions and a step-by-step version with pictures. They explain how to sign up for alerts that tell you when a document is recorded under your name, which matters for a vacant, inherited or rented house that nobody checks daily.

Records can also be searched through the online records link on the recorder's page, so a seller can pull up the last recorded deed, mortgage or lien before listing. Checking in advance helps the title company clear a mortgage that was paid off but never released, a common source of delay.

If you inherited a Highland County house, the deed or certificate may have been recorded long ago under a relative's name. Search the parcel before you promise a closing date to a buyer.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about selling in Highland County?
sections.html:
Highland County is hilly ground between the Little Miami and Scioto watersheds, organized in 1805 from parts of Ross, Adams and Clermont Counties. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts puts the 2025 population estimate at 43,823 and lists 19,196 housing units. Its 2020 to 2024 figures show a 74.3% owner-occupied rate, a median owner-occupied value of $168,900, median gross rent of $780 and median household income of $65,785.

The county's five school districts are Bright Local, Fairfield Local, Greenfield Exempted, Hillsboro City and Lynchburg-Clay Local, with the Laurel Oaks career campus and Southern State Community College nearby. Buyers ask about the district, so the deed's parcel number should be matched to the right one on the auditor's parcel search.

Non-city places named in the Census data include Buford, Highland Holiday and Rocky Fork Point, each a census-designated place in the county.

faqs.q: What is the cost to record a two-page deed in Highland County?
faqs.a: $39.00 under the rates effective January 1, 2025. Three pages cost $47.00, and the price rises $8.00 for each added page up to $103.00 at ten pages.

faqs.q: Does the Highland County Recorder take credit cards?
faqs.a: No. The recorder's page says recordings are cash or check only. Bring one of those to the Hillsboro office, and add a stamped, self-addressed envelope if you want the deed returned by mail.

faqs.q: What time do I need to arrive to have a deed recorded the same day?
faqs.a: Before 3:30 PM. The office is open until 4:00 PM, but documents received after 3:30 PM are held and recorded the next business day.

faqs.q: Why do I need to visit the auditor as well as the recorder?
faqs.a: Ohio law has the auditor review the statement of value and endorse the deed before it is recorded. Highland County sends the packet through the recorder, the auditor, the tax map office and back to the recorder.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed does not meet Ohio's document standards?
faqs.a: The recorder adds $20.00 to the recording charge for a nonconforming document notarized after July 1, 2009, and the tax map office or auditor may reject it for correction. Use black or blue ink and the required margins to avoid both.
